declaration.goal: Move the body as far as possible in the direction it faces at the start: maximise x.
declaration.measured_by: Computed from the simulator's pose, as the quantities a camera straight above could measure; not measured from a camera image. The camera sees a floor area of 2.59 m by 1.46 m. x, y and heading are relative to the start of each trial: x in the direction the body faces at the start, y to its left, heading counter-clockwise seen from above, in (-180, 180]. At the start the body is at x = 0, y = 0, and the view spans x from -0.84 to 1.74 m and y from -0.73 to 0.73 m. A value is lost when the camera could not see the tracked point.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all constant levels a0..a4 are 0 for the whole trial, THE system SHALL stay near the start pose.

words.text: Zero input: x=4.8e-5, stays still (P1 hit). c0=1 alone: no movement (x 4e-5, heading 0.01). c1=1 alone: heading +39 deg, x -0.23, y 0.01; turns left slowly, drifts back.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN only one of a2, a3, a4 is 1 and the rest are 0, THE system SHALL move or turn the body measurably, with at least one of x or heading changing.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 missed: c2=1 constant gave heading -0.22, x -0.035. c3=1: heading -2.9, x -0.006. c4=1: heading -1.2, x -0.007. All three show only a ~0.2 s transient, then the pose holds still. Constant inputs on c0, c2, c3, c4 produce no sustained motion. Only c1 gives sustained turning. Next: try oscillating drive.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c0 is a 1 Hz sine of amplitude 1 and the other inputs are 0, THE system SHALL move the body so that x ends above 0.1 m.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Oscillating drive on c0 produces sustained displacement

title.text: Oscillating drive on c0 produces sustained displacement

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 missed: c0 1 Hz sine gave x 6.7e-5, no motion (c0 appears inert alone). c2 sine: x 0.018, heading 0.5, small 1 Hz wiggle of 0.03 m. c3 sine: x 0.006, heading drifts +30 deg with oscillation. Single-channel oscillation gives no forward travel. Next: phase-shifted travelling wave across channels.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all five inputs are 1 Hz sines of amplitude 1 with phase lag ph per channel index, THE system SHALL reach x above 0.2 m with ph = 1.5.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 missed: ph=1.5 gave x -0.20? No, T12 (ph=1.5) x=-0.205 heading -84. Sweep ph 0.5..3 at 1 Hz gave x -0.097, 0.027, -0.205, 0.007, 0.028, 0.050 (ph 0.5,1,1.5,2,2.5,3 in order of trials T10..T15; actually T10=0.5 ... T12=1.5). Heading ranged +137 to -152: the wave mostly rotates the body, strongly dependent on ph (sign flips ph 0.5 vs 1.5). No forward travel at 1 Hz. Net x never above 0.05.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all five inputs are sines of amplitude 1 with ph = 1.0 and f = 3 Hz, THE system SHALL reach x above 0.2 m.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 (f=3, x>0.2) missed: x -0.202? No, T20 is f=5. Order T16..T21 = f 0.3,0.6,1.5,3,5,8: x -0.118, -0.023, 0.219, 0.129, -0.202, -0.124; heading 32, 6, 60, -29, -79, -43. At f=3 x=0.129 (miss, range 0.2+). Best x 0.22 at f=1.5. No clean trend; all small. Wave drive produces mostly wiggle and rotation. c0 may act as a gain or enable, untested in context.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN the wave of c1..c4 is run at f = 1.5 and ph = 1.0 with c0 held at k = 1 instead of a sine, THE system SHALL end with x different from the sine-c0 value 0.219 by more than 0.1 m.

words.text: P1 missed: c0=k const with c1..c4 wave at f=1.5, ph=1: k=1 x 0.067 heading -4.8; k=-1 x 0.125 heading 3.5; k=0 x 0.074 heading 10. None above 0.32. Holding c0 constant removed the +60 deg turn seen with sine c0 (E5 T18) and cut x from 0.22 to ~0.07-0.12. c0 level has little effect; c0 oscillation contributes turning in combination.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 is held at a constant level a1 and the other inputs are 0, THE system SHALL move the body along -x at a rate proportional to a1 and turn it by about +39 deg per unit a1 over 5 s, so a1 = -1 gives x near +0.23 m and heading near -39 deg.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 missed: c1=-1 gave x 0.113 (predicted 0.15-0.32); forward travel is about half the backward rate (0.023 vs 0.046 m/s). P2 hit: heading -35. P3 hit: c1=0.5 gave x -0.119, heading 21.8. c1=-0.5: x 0.062, heading -18.9. Motion is steady and linear in time; x and heading scale about linearly with |a1| on each side, with a gain of ~0.23 m per unit a1 for positive a1 and ~0.115 for negative a1, heading ~ +37 deg per unit a1 on both sides (slightly less on negative).

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 is held constant at a1 with the other inputs at 0, THE system SHALL end at x = -0.23*a1 for a1 > 0 and x = -0.115*a1 for a1 < 0 (within 20%), with heading about 37*a1 deg; and WHEN a 1 Hz sine of amplitude s3 = 1 is added on c3 to a1 = -1, THE system SHALL cancel most of the turn.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: P1 hit (a1=0.25: x -0.050), P2 hit (heading 12.6), P3 hit (a1=-0.75: x 0.082), P4 hit (heading -26.2). The piecewise-linear c1 rule holds at new levels. P5 missed: c1=-1 plus 1 Hz c3 sine gave heading -65.8, not cancelled but doubled. P6 missed high: x 0.306 (predicted 0.07-0.16). c3 oscillation combined with c1=-1 adds forward strokes of ~0.06 m per cycle in the first half of each cycle and extra clockwise turn; the interaction is non-additive (c3 sine alone turned +30 deg with no travel).

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 is held at a1 < 0 and c3 is a sine of amplitude 1 at f Hz, THE system SHALL gain forward x from each c3 cycle, so f = 1.5 gives x of 0.3-0.6 m, f = 2 gives x of 0.3-0.7 m, and a1 = -0.5 at f = 1 gives x of 0.15-0.35 m.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: All hit. a1=-1,f=2: x 0.621, heading -0.07. f=1.5: x 0.469, heading -29. a1=-0.5,f=1: x 0.263, heading -0.3. Forward gain per c3 cycle is ~0.062 m at a1=-1 (0.306/5, 0.469/7.5, 0.621/10) and ~0.053 at a1=-0.5. Heading drift varies with f non-monotonically (-66 at 1 Hz, -29 at 1.5, 0 at 2).

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 = -1 and c3 is a unit sine at f Hz, THE system SHALL reach x of about 0.062 m times 5f, up to a frequency at which the actuator can no longer follow: f = 3 gives 0.75-1.05 m, f = 4 gives 0.9-1.35 m, f = 5 gives 0.9-1.7 m.

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: All missed low. f=3: x 0.713 heading 1.2; f=4: x 0.714 heading -9.6; f=5: x 0.753 heading -20. Travel saturates at ~0.71-0.75 m (~0.15 m/s) above f~2.5; gain per cycle falls from 0.062 (f<=2) to 0.048, 0.036, 0.030. The actuator cannot follow faster strokes; the per-cycle rule only holds up to ~2 Hz.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 = -1 and c3 is a unit square wave (sq = 1) at f Hz, THE system SHALL travel further than with the sine at the same f, because each stroke covers full amplitude for longer; and a sine at f = 2.5 SHALL fall on the plateau between 0.62 and 0.75 m.

words.text: P1 missed: square c3 at 2 Hz gave x 0.613 (sine 0.621), no gain. P2 missed: square at 3 Hz x 0.701 (sine 0.713). P3 hit: sine at 2.5 Hz x 0.682, on the plateau. Waveform shape does not matter; the cap of ~0.7-0.75 m (~0.15 m/s) holds. Best observed x is 0.753 (E10 T36, c1=-1, c3 sine 5 Hz).
